finding.claim: Subscriber-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and later POSTed to by the server, giving full SSRF. An attacker can target internal services, loopback or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and the payload is sent to the attacker-chosen host.
finding.source: callbackUrl body parameter of POST /subscribe (Jobs.subscribe, line 13)

trace.note: stored unvalidated in the subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates the stored URLs every minute
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no scheme, host or IP checks
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking or DNS pinning anywhere on the path. subscribe() does no validation, and notifyAll() does none before sending. The response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF. The attacker still controls the destination and can trigger internal POST requests.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 builds URI.create(cb) and calls client.send with no scheme/host/IP checks (the only regex guard, line 30, is in the unrelated thumb()). The route and scheduler aren't in the repo, so the per-minute trigger and any auth on POST /subscribe are known only from comments.
